To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high salt transiently increases nitric oxide (NO) production and NO synthase-3 (NOS3, also known as endothelial NO synthetase) expression, but that the increase in NO production is dissociated from NOS3 expression.

a high-salt diet increases NOS3 activity in the thick ascending limb of Henle's loop but that this increase is not due to increased expression of the NOS3 gene or to changes in the availability of cofactors.
HS transiently increases NOS3 activity, expression, and NO production, but, over time, these processes dissociate because of changes in NOS phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nitric oxide (NO) in the thick ascending limb of Henle's loop (THAL).
how a high-salt diet alters the expression and activity of the endothelial nitric oxide synthase in the thick ascending limb of the kidney.
the mechanisms by which dietary sodium alters sodium transport by the THAL and how these changes are regulated by NO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HS increases NO production in THAL, but the mechanism by which HS increases THAL-NOS is not clear at the present time.
a high-salt diet dissociates NOS3 expression from NO production by the thick ascending limbs by changes in NOS phosphorylation.
HS acutely stimulates THAL NO release and that this is mediated by NOS3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NOS3 expression is regulated by HS but not NO production, and the mechanism is via changes in NOS phosphorylation.
HS increases THAL NO production by a mechanism involving changes in NOS phosphorylation and superoxide levels that dissociates NO production from expression.
the THAL is able to adapt to HS by increasing NO production and that this is mediated by changes in NOS phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acute effect of HS on THAL NO production is mediated by NOS3 phosphorylations and not by expression.
the acute effect of HS is to increase THAL NOS activity, which is dissociated by chronic HS.
the acute increase in NO release by HS is not due to increased NOS3 expression but rather to a change in the phosphorylation state of the enzyme, resulting in increased activity and release of NO.
